checks.observed: The merge guard asked 64 times across 31 sessions (app-a 34, app-b 12, app-c 6, app-d 4, app-e 1, other 7). 58 were approved and ran, 6 ran and failed for unrelated reasons, none were declined. 56 of the 64 were long chained commands; about 7 matched merge text inside a heredoc or script being written. The helper logged 85 refusals: push to main 24 (all but 5 from 0.12.x), task record in another worktree 11, unstated blocking findings 9, CI for a different commit 8.
evidence: Transcript hook_success attachments with permissionDecision ask, joined by toolUseID to Bash tool_use and tool_result.
jq over ~/.local/state/solo-workflow/helper.jsonl grouped by command, reason and version.

checks.observed: The app-e command returned ask from the 0.14.2 hook and nothing (no prompt) from the new one. All 66 commands that got the prompt historically return nothing from the new hook.
evidence: sh old-guard.sh < app-e-input.json -> permissionDecision ask; new hook -> empty output, exit 0.

checks.observed: app-e, app-a, app-b and app-d have an active required-checks ruleset with no bypass actors (current_user_can_bypass: never), so GitHub refuses any merge before checks pass. app-c has no required-checks ruleset. The new hook denies gh pr merge --admin without prompting.
evidence: App-e command with --admin appended -> permissionDecision deny.

checks.observed: Agents passed --blocking-findings none 17 times; the helper now reads it as zero. Unstated, empty or malformed counts are still refused.
evidence: tests/helpers/delivery.test.ts: 62 pass, including the new 'none' case.

findings.summary: The merge guard returned permissionDecision ask, which Claude Code shows as a prompt in every permission mode, Bypass included. It never checked CI itself, and the owner approved every answered prompt, so it added a stop without adding safety where GitHub already requires checks.
evidence: Claude Code hooks docs: ask prompts the user; deny blocks in every mode including bypassPermissions.

findings.summary: Finish said never to run gh pr merge by hand, yet agents did so 64+ times with --match-head-commit, which is safe where a ruleset requires checks. The rule was routinely broken rather than followed.
evidence: Most guarded commands used gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit <sha>.

findings.summary: Three background rg scans with no path argument waited on stdin forever and were killed; rerun with an explicit path and </dev/null they finished in minutes.
evidence: ps: rg processes at 0% CPU and 0:00 time after several minutes.

interventions: The owner asked why the background scans were taking so long, which exposed that they were hung.
limitations: Single arm: no run without the plugin to compare against.
Prompt outcomes are inferred from tool results; a prompt answered 'no' could look like a missing result, but none were missing.
app-c has no required-checks ruleset, so there a direct merge relies on the agent having read the checks.
